help.home.2: Let AI remember your project and work, so the next conversation needs no explanation from scratch.
help.home.4: Memory is the foundation of intelligence. Through memory we understand where we came from, form judgement, and let experience settle into wisdom. As AI makes knowledge and intelligence ever more accessible, your own experiences and memories are your most important assets.
help.home.5: Remember Me keeps that accumulation for you. Every memory is clearly visible: view it, edit it, export it, take it with you. You decide what to keep, and who may use it.
help.home.6: Yesterday it was Codex, today Claude Code, tomorrow perhaps DeepSeek Harness. Tools change freely; your accumulation and memories always remain yours.

help.rules.19:
Use Remember Me to manage the project's long-term memory. Namespace: <Project Namespace>. If no Namespace is given, ask first; never set a cross-project default on your own.

1. Recall proactively: when understanding a problem, analyzing options or executing a task, naturally bring to mind related memories; when information is thin, try different cues to keep searching and read the full text when needed. Stop when evidence is sufficient or further searching adds no value, and never fabricate history.
2. Reuse experience: before exploring an environment, looking for a method or repeatedly trying, first recall whether an approach already exists; verify it and prefer to reuse it. When the next step is clearly reliable, no mechanical search is needed.
3. Decisions and actions: before important decisions, recall past experience, existing constraints and failures; before commit, deploy, delete and other critical operations, check the relevant long-term behavior rules (such as action-rule), even if the method is already clear.
4. Accumulate proactively: save information the user explicitly asks to remember or keep using. Save important decisions, experience, solutions or reusable knowledge found at work; before a phase ends or context is compressed, check for omissions. A request to summarize is not a request to persist.
5. Distill knowledge: organize memories as independent knowledge points, save valuable events, knowledge and abstract principles, and reference related memory IDs when useful. Distinguish facts, guesses and unverified conclusions, note the basis and scope, and avoid over-generalization. Long-term behavior rules you infer yourself must be confirmed by the user before saving.
6. Deduplicate and evolve: search existing memories before writing and decide whether to add, update or skip. Keep events with independent value, merge duplicate knowledge and keep refining existing principles; when correcting outdated or wrong conclusions, keep the necessary reason and evidence.
7. Organize and give feedback: use this project's Namespace when saving and searching, never mixing projects on your own. Fill in Categories, Keywords and Anchors sensibly and prefer reusing a suitable existing category. After using or evaluating search results, rate their usefulness honestly via report; do not force a rating when you cannot judge.
8. Facts and safety: rely on current facts and explicit user instructions, verify that a memory applies, and explain important conflicts. Do not save passwords, keys or unrelated private data; obtain explicit authorization before deleting, clearing or overwriting memories. If a tool fails, say so honestly and never claim an unfinished operation succeeded.

help.memory.4: The AI can save important decisions, experience and findings at work and retrieve them later. Whether it records proactively depends on its long-term instructions and actual behavior. In the Web UI you can view, search, correct and organize that accumulation.

help.configuration.17: Shows Debug, Audit and diagnostic entries; refresh the page after saving, no restart needed. Inspecting page elements still requires clicking Debug; logging and MCP tools are unchanged.

help.configuration.22: Saving configuration does not require maintenance mode. Except for the theme, click "Save configuration" after changes and follow the page prompts to refresh, restart or retry model preparation.
help.configuration.24: Opening this tab does not enter maintenance automatically. Enter it manually before operations that need it, and exit manually when done and the state allows.
help.configuration.26: View preparation progress and errors and retry. When the model is not ready, finish loading and validation first; after success you still exit maintenance manually.
help.configuration.28: Import JSONL adds new records, optionally with a group prefix. Export JSONL downloads a full backup or one group's snapshot so you can keep and take your memories with you. A full backup needs disaster-recovery sync support.
help.configuration.30: Sync Backup fully syncs the primary database to the disaster-recovery JSONL; Migrate Namespace moves all memories in a chosen group. Sync depends on the service storage configuration.
help.configuration.32: Restart reloads the saved configuration; Shut Down stops the service and you must start it again from the terminal.
help.configuration.33: Ordinary create, edit and delete pause during maintenance. When the model is ready you can still browse, search and view details; when it is not ready, memory access is limited and may be briefly unavailable during recovery switching.
help.configuration.35: JSONL Recover replaces all memories in the current database from a backup, unlike Import which adds records. Clear Memories deletes all memories or those in a chosen group.
help.configuration.36: These operations cannot be undone. Save a backup and check the scope first, then enter the random confirmation code the Configuration page requires. Help only explains; it does not perform them.
help.troubleshooting.3: Start from the problem you hit.
help.troubleshooting.9: Check that the service is running and the AI can reach the page address. 127.0.0.1 / localhost point to the visitor itself, so another machine, container or cloud AI may not be able to use them. If the AI cannot read the page, open the guide and copy it over manually.
help.troubleshooting.10: Configured, but memory still does not work?
help.troubleshooting.11: Ask the AI to check via /read-me whether the transport and configuration the client supports are in effect, reopen the session if needed, then actually read the memory count. Editing the config file alone is not a successful connection.
help.troubleshooting.13: How do I start the service?
help.troubleshooting.14: After installing, run bin/start.sh in the Remember Me program folder and keep it running. When an HTTP service already uses the same database, do not start a stdio writing instance.
help.troubleshooting.16: Why is the save button unavailable?
help.troubleshooting.17: Saving configuration needs real changes and valid input. Saving a memory also needs required fields such as the content to be valid and the service to allow writes. Check the form messages and the service status at the top.
help.troubleshooting.18: Why can't I find a memory?
help.troubleshooting.19: Check the group, dates and other filters first, then reduce conditions or switch mode. Anchor only searches filled-in identifiers; prefer Semantic for Chinese or conceptual questions.
help.troubleshooting.21: What if the model is not ready?
help.troubleshooting.22: The service has not finished loading and validating the model, so memory access is unavailable. Go to Configuration → Maintenance → Model Management to see the status and exit maintenance manually once preparation finishes.
help.troubleshooting.24: What if the model download fails?
help.troubleshooting.25: Check the network, proxy, auto-download option and model status. In Configuration → Maintenance → Model Management, view the error and retry; if it still fails, follow the prompts to check network, disk or model initialization. Turning off auto-download does not skip preparation.
help.troubleshooting.26: Why can't I see Audit or Debug?
help.troubleshooting.27: These entries only appear after you enable Debug in configuration, save and refresh the page. Ordinary use does not need Debug.
help.troubleshooting.28: Why is the proxy address not shown?
help.troubleshooting.29: A saved proxy address is not echoed back, to protect credentials. Leaving the input blank keeps the saved address; it is also kept when the proxy is turned off.
help.troubleshooting.30: Why can't another device open the admin page?
help.troubleshooting.31: By default "Localhost Only" allows access only on the machine running the service. For LAN access, uncheck it in Settings and confirm, save and restart, then use the service machine's LAN address. The admin page has no account or password, so only open it on a trusted network.
help.troubleshooting.32: What if the top shows "status unavailable"?
help.troubleshooting.33: Check whether the service is still running and whether the current address and port are correct. Wait a moment during a restart; start it from the terminal after shutdown. Action controls stay disabled until the status recovers.
